name: Janes landing page for its open source defence and security intelligence service
title: Janes landing page for its open source defence and security intelligence service
answer: This is the landing page for Janes, a long-running subscription provider of open source defence and security intelligence. It describes how Janes gathers information through human specialists, verifies every data point against vetted sources, peer reviews final content, and connects millions of data points so customers can move from what happened to what it means. The most useful point for a defence reader is that Janes positions its validated data as foundational input for planning, analysis and forecasting, and for the Joint Intelligence Preparation of the Operational Environment process.

sections.body: Janes publishes this page as the entry point to its open source defence and security intelligence service. It is a commercial product landing page rather than a report, study or dataset, and it carries no publication date. Its scope is the company's own offering, covering military platforms, threat intelligence, industry awareness and advisory services, delivered through a subscription portal or fused into a customer's own system. The page describes method and intended use in general terms and sets out no coverage lists, pricing or delivery schedules.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Janes presents itself as a trusted source for defence intelligence, applying what it calls proven tradecraft to produce validated intelligence so teams can move from fragmented reporting to a defensible, connected view of capability, intent and risk. The company says its experts collect information from vetted on-the-ground and industry specialists, exclusive interviews and events, describing them as human sensors gathering data no web crawler could access. Raw information is turned into understanding through deep expertise, transparent analytic tradecraft, imagery analysis and advanced modelling. Janes states that every data point is verified against reliable, vetted sources under strict credibility criteria, and that final content is peer reviewed to meet a decision-grade standard. It describes its holdings as the largest global dataset of its type, governed rigorously and connected by advanced technology to reveal patterns, signals and trajectories. Customers can access the validated data in the Janes portal or fuse it with other sources in their own systems, to plan, analyse and forecast. The page says Janes supports the Joint Intelligence Preparation of the Operational Environment process and lets analysts approach any intelligence question from any direction, understanding connections between actors, equipment and events for course of action analysis. A demonstration shows navigation through validated data in the portal.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, dates or financial figures. Its specific claims are qualitative: that Janes holds the largest global dataset of its type, that every data point is verified against vetted sources, that final content is peer reviewed, that its experts act as human sensors collecting data no web crawler could access, and that its intelligence is unclassified and shareable across domains and partners.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in defence would use this page mainly as a pointer to a data source rather than as evidence about AI. Janes is named on the industry page as one of the long-running providers covering the defence-industrial base, and this landing page confirms the company sells subscription access to validated defence and security data that can be fused into a customer's own systems. That fusion point is where the source is relevant to AI work, because validated, structured defence data is the kind of input analytics and modelling pipelines depend on. The page itself does not discuss artificial intelligence, machine learning or autonomy, so it supports the claim that Janes exists and describes its method, not any claim about AI capability.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Defense

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page with no date, no methodology detail, no coverage lists, no pricing and no named customers. It does not mention contractors, programmes or procurement forecasts, so it does not substantiate the industry page's description of Janes as maintaining databases of contractors, programmes and procurement forecasts. It also says nothing about artificial intelligence. The claims about verification, peer review and dataset size are the company's own and are not evidenced here. A reader wanting substance on defence-industrial coverage or on AI in defence should go to Janes product documentation or independent sources.
